perspective:
**Alice Lim’s accessible perspective:**

- She knows Austin as an old friend from high school; they are close and discuss their personal and professional lives. She knows he has an office/work situation.
- She noticed Austin had become reserved when work came up. Concerned and curious, she invited him for coffee.
- She asked if everything was okay at the office. Austin said it was “nothing really,” just “usual ups and downs.” When she pressed, he said he wasn’t sure how to handle “a few things at work” and that it was “complicated.” She received no specific details.
- From this, she believed he might be hiding something about his job performance, and later believed he might be considering a career change due to dissatisfaction. She felt worried about his well-being.
- She asked if he had thought about changing careers. Austin said he had, but was unsure what other paths he could take, and asked for her suggestion.
- She suggested healthcare, offered to tell him about her experiences, and offered to connect him with contacts. Austin said it sounded interesting and wanted to know more.
- She sensed he was hesitant and afraid of the unknown; she felt frustration and empathy. She told him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and was happier. Austin said that was inspiring but he worried about risks and initial struggle.
- She told him such feelings were natural, growth comes from stepping out of comfort zones, and she would support him. Austin thanked her and said it helped to have her support and hear real success stories.
- She offered to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. Austin said that would be helpful and appreciated her help. She said she would set up a meeting next week; Austin thanked her and said he looked forward to it.
- She felt encouraged and hopeful after seeing his openness.
- After several discussions/meetings, she believed Austin was ready for next steps and appreciated her help. She felt satisfaction and joy.
- She told him she was proud and asked how he felt. Austin said he felt excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful. She suggested regular check-ins; Austin agreed, saying it would keep him focused and that her perspective helps.
- She plans regular check-ins with Austin to discuss his progress and challenges.
